title: fix(cloud-workers): preserve replacement owners during forced abandonment
body:
Related: #165957

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes forced worker abandonment failing a replacement placement or discarding its pending workspace result when cleanup resumes after the session's owner changes.

## User Impact

A replacement turn keeps its placement, claim, tools, and pending workspace result when delayed cleanup for the previous owner resumes. Ordinary forced abandonment still closes its own tool admission, joins entered work, and records the abandoned result.

If ownership changes at the native transition boundary, teardown rejects the stale operation rather than taking over the replacement. Operators can retry against the current owner. Filesystem rollback remains best effort; failed rollback journals remain available for recovery. No schema, configuration, or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

On base `472b7f94d52d`, `placement-force-abandon.ts:112` rereads the reconciliation inventory after awaited journal/result work and then tears down whichever placement it finds. `placement-transitions.worker.ts:123` checks the placement tuple but has no caller-captured turn constraint, so a replacement claim at the same generation can be cleared.

Capture the selected placements and claims once, close their tool admission before cleanup preparation, preserve changed owners and their artifacts, and carry the original claim or claimlessness through the existing drain/reconcile transactions. Reconciliation reuses the existing exact-claim predicate. Main's returned-row optimization remains intact. This is independent of the session-controller changes in #165957.

The simplification pass retained the existing placement, tool-admission, and SQLite writer owners; it adds no controller, scheduler, persistent state, or compatibility path. Production delta: **+127/-10 (net +117)**. Test delta: **+245/-44 (net +201)**. Documentation: one existing paragraph clarified. The production growth captures ownership across awaits and supplies the missing transaction guard.

## Evidence

The Team audit's 978,202-line journal contains 23 shutdown-deadline records, four naming worker-placement reconciliation (lines 827529, 846227, 871857, 976432). The final example and exit are sanitized below:

```text
L976432 2026-10-15T06:58:28.408Z [gateway] shutdown deadline reached; pending close steps: shutdown.connection-dependent-sidecars=57223ms, shutdown.worker-placement.reconcile=57222ms; cleanup incomplete
L976437 2026-10-15T06:58:30Z openclaw-gateway.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```

These establish delayed cleanup pressure, not production attribution to this particular bug. The deterministic reproduction establishes the defect independently: on unchanged base production code, **7 tests failed and 8 passed**. Replacement epoch, placement, and claim cases changed the successor from active to failed and cleared its claim; all four native-transition controls completed when they should have rejected. With this repair, all 16 abandonment tests pass, including the later released-claim regression.

Focused proof (all with `TMPDIR` set to a short task-specific directory):

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-turn-claims.worker.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-store.turn-claim-closure.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-move-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-abandon-lifecycle.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/device-folder-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
pnpm tsgo:core
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts"]'
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-transitions.worker.ts
pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-transitions.worker.ts docs/gateway/cloud-workers/session-lifecycle.md
git diff --check
```

The six-suite run passed **102/102 tests**, 625.85s including cold worker compilation. The initial abandonment file's 15 cases used 44.743s of test time on a heavily loaded Mac; real SQLite worker admission, closure, and artifact recovery are necessary to prove this boundary. The selected Gateway test typecheck passed in 33.0s. Production typecheck, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. No test timeout or budget changed. CI timing will be reported after the final-head run.

An initial test-harness edit used an unsupported `it.each` context parameter; that was corrected before the valid red/green reproduction above. No live Gateway or Team state was touched.

GitHub review identified one additional P2 case: a captured claim can finish normally during cleanup preparation. A deterministic test reproduced the active placement being left behind; the comparison now permits a released claim while still rejecting a replacement claim, and the native write uses the existing unclaimed guard. After that correction, the abandonment, move-abandonment, and retained-cleanup lifecycle suites passed **50/50 tests** in 242.77s; its 16 abandonment cases used 40.317s of test time. The unchanged native-transition, claim-closure, and device-folder proofs from the first run remain applicable. Production and selected-test typechecks, lint, and formatting passed again.

Follow-up proof:

```sh
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'handles a release change'
pnpm test src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-force-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-move-abandon.test.ts src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-abandon-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The first command failed before the correction and passed as part of the full file afterward. Both runtime proof rounds used the real database workers with deterministic timing gates, not sleeps.

Fresh Codex autoreview of final head `87d6e00ce224b`: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings. Final-head [CI run 38983022533](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38983022533) completed successfully for `87d6e00ce224b4c3d56ff6efa0e977fec06075a6` in 12m03s. The exact-head watcher returned **GREEN**, zero pending checks, and 15 superseded entries. No current-head failures remain; superseded historical entries can still color GitHub's aggregate rollup red. ClawSweeper's final-head re-review found no actionable defects and marked the PR ready for maintainer review. The earlier released-claim thread is resolved. This PR remains open and unmerged for lead review.
